content: 1. Administer 6 mL of the medication orally every 6 hours after meals and at bedtime. Do not exceed a total daily dose of 480 mg for individuals over 12 years of age. For this age group, the dosage can range from 40 mg to 360 mg orally every 6 hours after meals and at bedtime, with a maximum daily dose of 500 mg. 2. Loose stools may occur as a side effect. Hypersensitivity to simethicone is a contraindication for use. 3. Chewable tablets must be thoroughly chewed before swallowing. Liquid-filled capsules should not be chewed. 4. This medication may interfere with gastric guaiac tests, potentially causing false-negative results. 5. During pregnancy, simethicone is classified as Category C. It is not systemically absorbed and is not expected to be excreted in breast milk. 6. Simethicone works by altering the surface tension of gas bubbles, causing foam bubbles to collapse. This facilitates the passage of gas and prevents the formation of gas pockets in the gastrointestinal tract. 7. The drug is excreted unchanged in the feces, with complete elimination occurring within 24 to 48 hours. 8. Simethicone is commonly marketed under brand names such as Mylicon and is used to alleviate symptoms of excessive gas caused by swallowing air or consuming certain foods or infant formulas. 9. Always check the product label for ingredients, even if you have used the product before, as manufacturers may change the formulation. Products with similar names may contain different ingredients intended for different purposes. 10. Follow all instructions on the product packaging. If prescribed by a doctor, administer the medication as directed. Typically, it is given orally as needed after meals and at bedtime. 11. The dosage is determined based on the child’s age, medical condition, and response to treatment. Do not increase the dose or administer the product more frequently than directed. 12. Shake the container well before each use. Measure the dose carefully using a special measuring device or dropper. Avoid using household spoons, as they may not provide an accurate dose. 13. Administer the liquid slowly by mouth, aiming for the inside of the cheek to prevent spitting or choking. Alternatively, the dose may be mixed with 1 ounce (30 mL) of cool water, infant formula, or juice. Mix well and administer immediately. 14. Simethicone generally has no side effects. If prescribed by a doctor, it is because the benefits outweigh the risks. Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare. 15. If you are in the U.S. and experience side effects, contact your doctor for medical advice. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. 16. Before administering simethicone, inform the doctor or pharmacist if your child is allergic to it or has any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. 17. This form of simethicone is not typically used by adults and is unlikely to be used during pregnancy or breastfeeding. 18. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all products your child uses, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. 19. Simethicone may reduce the absorption of thyroid medications, such as levothyroxine. 20. In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms like loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. 21. If a dose is missed and the medication is taken on a regular schedule, administer it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with the regular schedule. Do not double the dose. 22. Store the medication at room temperature, away from moisture, heat, and light. Do not freeze it or store it in the bathroom. 23. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard the product when it is expired or no longer needed. 24. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about the product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your child. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your child’s specific health needs.
